arguments.content:
The three load-bearing tensions Anthony originally flagged for collaborative pressure-testing in the cannabis evidence report (circa 2026-05-18):

1. Pain indication: NASEM 2017 said “substantial evidence,” the 2026 Cochrane update says no clear evidence, and Wang et al. sits in between with a real-but-small effect. Held all three rather than resolving it — the spot where a collaborator might legitimately push to either commit or sharpen the disagreement into something falsifiable.

2. Schizophrenia causality framing: “probable component cause, not provable absent unethical randomization” — the strongest harm claim in the document and the one most vulnerable to both overstatement and motivated dismissal. Leaned on Bradford Hill rather than asserting causation outright. Worth pressure-testing whether that’s the right epistemic resting place or a hedge.

3. Entourage effect: Called it hypothesis-not-proof on the strength of the Cooper 2013 double-dummy null and the 2024 PRISMA review. Defensible but a relatively thin human-evidence base to hang a negative conclusion on, and the claim most likely to draw substantive disagreement from anyone who knows the in vitro literature.
